intro: Shiloh's ministry has never stopped at the sanctuary door. Through the Faith Community Development Corporation — chartered by Shiloh and led by Pastor McCluster — the church has spent decades working on housing, economic development, sustainability, and justice for the City of Bridgeport.

items.title: The church that stood in the way — and won
items.body: United Illuminating's Docket 516R plan would have run high-voltage transmission monopoles through Bridgeport and Fairfield's residential and historic districts — threatening Shiloh's own building and the historic Mary & Eliza Freeman Houses. Anchored by Pastor McCluster, 85-year-old Shiloh became ground zero for the community's stand. Residents and clergy were joined by a bipartisan delegation including Senator Tony Hwang, Representative Jennifer Leeper, city council members, and Freeman Center president Maisa Tisdale, raising transparency and environmental-justice concerns the process had ignored.
items.outcome: On October 16, 2025 the Connecticut Siting Council voted 5–3 to deny the application. UI asked the Council to reconsider; on February 5, 2026 the Council rejected that appeal and closed Docket 516R. The community's unified front was recognized as a major factor in the decision.

items.title: The first African-American church in Connecticut to go solar
items.body: Committed to sustainability, Pastor McCluster led Shiloh to become the first African-American church in the State of Connecticut to become energy self-sufficient through solar power. Shiloh is cited as a recognized Connecticut leader in the EPA's "God Goes Green" initiative, and the milestone is listed as the lead accomplishment of Freedom, Inc.'s sustainability work.

items.title: Faith Community Development Corporation
items.body: Chartered by Shiloh Baptist Church and led by Pastor McCluster as its President, Faith CDC carries the church's work into housing, economic development, and capacity building — training faith-based organizations nationwide in governance, program design, and revenue that renews itself, so a mission outlasts any single grant.

items.title: Bridgeport Regional Sustainability Summit
items.body: Shiloh hosted part of the 7th Annual Bridgeport Regional Sustainability Summit — "Learning to breathe easier and build better" — a full day of community training, a clergy luncheon, and an evening community conversation, held with the University of Bridgeport.
